want.now.why: No yo: the -o ending on quiero already says I, so the subject is fused into the door. aprender follows directly, with no word for to.

want.past.why: Tense goes into the door: quería is the imperfect, the usual past for a wish. Quise (preterite) would suggest I tried or decided to.

want.neg.why: No do-support: no simply goes in front of the conjugated verb, and nothing else changes.

want.q.why: Same words as a statement; only the -es ending (tú), the opening ¿ and rising pitch make it a question. No tú needed.

decline.now.why: Spanish says ir, not venir, when you are declining to go to the other person's event. tengo que is the have-to door; both subjects are in the verb endings.

decline.past.why: Two different pasts: pude (preterite) for the one failed event, tenía que (imperfect) for the background obligation.

decline.fut.why: Spoken future is ir a + infinitive: voy a carries tense and person, so poder and tener que become infinitives. No podré ir is the written option.

decline.although.why: aunque + indicative (tengo) states a real fact. aunque tenga que, with the subjunctive, would mean even if I have to.

like.now.why: Flipped like Hindi: literally coffee pleases me. Me marks the liker, and gusta agrees with el café, the grammatical subject.

like.neg.why: no must come before me, not between me and gusta. The article el stays: coffee in general.

like.she.why: gusta does not change, because coffee is still the subject; only me becomes le. A ella is added for clarity, since le alone could be he or you.

like.q.why: te marks tú as the liker; the words are the same as a statement and only intonation and ¿? make it a question.

go.habit.why: voy is irregular ir with I built in. a + el fuses into al, so al mercado is one unit, as in French au marché.

go.prog.why: Plain present voy plus ahorita (right now, common in Latin America) does the job. Estoy yendo exists but sounds odd for a trip.

go.past.why: fui is one word carrying I, go and past: the preterite of ir, which is identical to the preterite of ser (I was).

go.fut.why: voy a ir: go-to-go. The future sits on voy a, and the main verb ir is repeated as an infinitive. Mañana voy al mercado is just as common.

go.neg.why: No aux, no -ing: no before the plain present voy covers I am not going.

live.now.why: Present vivo, not a perfect: hace dos años (it makes two years) carries the since-then meaning. Llevo dos años viviendo aquí is the other common way.

live.past.why: Finished stretch: preterite viví, and the duration is bare dos años with no preposition. Only the accent and stress move from vivo to viví.

live.fut.why: No future perfect: cumplir (complete) takes the tense via voy a, and viviendo follows. Habré vivido exists but sounds written.

live.q.why: llevar + gerund is the spoken have-been-ing: llevas holds tú and the ongoing time, viviendo the verb. ¿Hace cuánto vives aquí? also works.

if.real.why: si + present, ir a + infinitive in the main clause. Viajaré or plain viajo are also heard. Never a future after si.

if.unreal.why: Four words: tuviera (imperfect subjunctive) after si, and the -ía ending on viajaría does the work of I would. Tuviese is the rarer variant.

if.past.why: Both clauses use haber + participle: hubiera tenido, habría viajado. In speech hubiera viajado often replaces habría in the main clause too.
